clue.text: Late professor's nephew as knight errant

indicators.note: errant means wandering or straying, so these letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: A dead academic's nephew rides out like a knight seeking adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'errant' looks like part of the phrase 'knight errant' but shuffles NEPHEW AS KNIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist who died in 2018 held the Lucasian chair at Cambridge, so he is a late professor.

clue.text: Honorary Tory leader implicated in kinky ritual

indicators.note: to be implicated in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece goes within the other
kinky means twisted, so the letters of ritual are twisted round
the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of Tory

explanation.surface: A politician with an honorary post is caught up in some perverse ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' turns RITUAL into TIULAR, and 'implicated in' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular post is held in name only, an honorary title without real duties.

clue.text: Point out a winemaker

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of point are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is pointing out a particular wine producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a grape variety, and grapes are what make wine, so playfully it is a winemaker.

clue.text: Illustration no longer sufficient?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was, as in ex-wife
ample means enough, sufficient

explanation.surface: A question whether a picture has stopped being adequate.
explanation.definitionFit: An example illustrates a point, so an illustration is an example given to explain something.

clue.text: See 1
Last, but not first, swimmer is off course

indicators.note: the word Last is taken but without its first letter

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: The last swimmer in a race has gone off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means wandering away from the right path, off course.

clue.text: Kittens to play — getting most tangled

indicators.note: to play is to frolic about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Playful kittens get the wool into the worst tangles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' belongs in the fodder, not the indicator: KITTENS TO is rearranged by 'play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotty means full of knots, so the superlative is the most tangled.

clue.text: Impossible bottle party?

definitions.meaning: a colloquial refusal meaning it cannot be done
a playful reading: a do (party) where there is no can (bottle) to be had

explanation.surface: A party where bringing a bottle turns out to be impossible.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for a flat refusal, saying a request is impossible; the second reading splits it as no can plus do, a party.

clue.text: At first, cinemagoer natters rudely during tear-jerker, causing dismay

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of cinemagoer
during means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an onion makes your eyes water, a jokey tear-jerker

indicators.note: rudely means roughly or crudely, so the letters of natters are roughed up

explanation.surface: A cinemagoer chatting loudly through a weepie upsets everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear-jerker' suggests a sad film, but here it is the vegetable that makes eyes water; 'rudely' and 'during' are the anagram and insertion signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is a feeling of anxious shock, which is what dismay means.

clue.text: Shock as tabloid pinches Telegraph leader

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip or take, so the tabloid holds a letter inside it

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter, here of Telegraph

explanation.surface: A newspaper scandal: one paper steals a rival's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' misleads as a newspaper editorial; here it is just the first letter. The Telegraph is a British broadsheet.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or astonish them into silence.

clue.text: Patsy forced to fast? Finishes off Limoncello, Cointreau, cognac and Scotch

indicators.note: forced means pushed out of shape, so the letters of to fast are bent into a new order
the finishes of the listed drinks are their last letters

explanation.surface: Someone told to fast instead finishes off a range of liqueurs and spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' makes ASOFTT from TO FAST; then come O, U, C and H from the drinks' ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft touch is someone easily persuaded or taken advantage of, which is what a patsy is.

clue.text: Feel empty, needing compassion over dump

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outer letters, its middle gone
over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pity is compassion

explanation.surface: Feeling hollow and needing sympathy after being dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PITY into YTIP. Fly-tipping is the British term for illegally dumping rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly-tip is to dump rubbish illegally somewhere public.

clue.text: Irritated seeing rat outside shopping centre

indicators.note: one piece goes outside, around the other

parts.note: to rat is to inform on, and in slang to sing is to do the same
a mart is a market, a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed to see a rat outside the mall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' is a verb, to inform, giving SING, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarting means stung and resentful, feeling irritated.

clue.text: Not seeing straight when angry, I'd say

parts.note: cross means angry

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so we want something that sounds like them

parts.note: the contraction I'd, spoken, gives the sound of eyed

explanation.surface: Someone claims anger makes them see wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-eyed describes eyes turned inward, so a person cannot look straight.

clue.text: Initially terrified, Warhol is being treated for poor hearing

indicators.note: something being treated is being worked on, so these letters are processed into a new order
initially takes the first letter of terrified

explanation.surface: A frightened Andy Warhol is receiving treatment for deafness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor hearing' looks medical, but a hearing is a trial. Fodder is T plus WARHOL IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A show trial is a staged legal hearing whose verdict is fixed in advance, a poor excuse for justice.

clue.text: Emotion not in order for this movement

indicators.note: not takes the letters of in away from the anagram pool
to put in order is to rearrange, so the remaining letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep feelings out of things for the sake of a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: EMOTION without I and N leaves EMOTO, which 'order' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The campaign against sexual harassment that spread on social media in 2017 is known by this name.

clue.text: Criminal humanoid turned fine

indicators.note: turned means reversed, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an orc is a humanoid monster in fantasy fiction
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A humanoid robot is turned into a fine figure, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ORC to give CRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a dishonest person, a criminal.

clue.text: Encounter with Mac could become unromantic

indicators.note: could become signals that the answer and Mac together could be rearranged into the word unromantic

explanation.surface: A date with someone called Mac could turn out unromantic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters plus MAC rearrange into UNROMANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance, to encounter them.

clue.text: Insect, say, flying over the moon

indicators.note: flying means scattered about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An insect taking flight over the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the moon' looks literal, a bug flying high, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the moon is an idiom for delighted, and in ecstasy means overjoyed.

clue.text: Sweet is almost entirely à la crème pudding

indicators.note: a pudding is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up
almost entirely means all but the final letter of à la crème

explanation.surface: A dessert said to be almost wholly made with cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' drops the last E, leaving ALACREM, which 'pudding' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a toffee-like confection, a sweet.

clue.text: Thief working separately without pay

indicators.note: without means the letters of pay are left out of the pool
working means set in motion, so the remaining letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A thief operates alone and takes no wages.
explanation.walkthrough: SEPARATELY without P, A and Y leaves SERATEL, which 'working' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A stealer is one who steals, a thief.

clue.text: Junior doctor for Bury and Wigan at last

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of Wigan

explanation.surface: A trainee medic covering for two Lancashire towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury and Wigan look like neighbouring towns in Greater Manchester; Bury is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage an intern is a hospital doctor in early training.

clue.text: Tintin's struggling with Haddock's sixth sense

indicators.note: struggling means floundering about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Haddock is Captain Haddock in the Tintin books, and C abbreviates captain

explanation.surface: Tintin and Captain Haddock relying on intuition in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haddock' looks like the fish but is Tintin's friend Captain Haddock, giving C.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth sense is intuition, knowing without reasoning, which is instinct.

clue.text: Rue de Pierre Gretzky

indicators.note: de is French for from or of, so the answer is taken from within these words

explanation.surface: A French street name honouring someone called Pierre Gretzky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rue' looks like the French for street, as 'de' suggests, but is the English verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it.

clue.text: Ditch solving Sudoku — all real silly in the end

indicators.note: in the end applies to each word in turn, taking its last letter

explanation.surface: Giving up on a Sudoku that is all completely silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solving' is not a link word: its final G starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully is a channel cut by water, a ditch or gutter.

clue.text: Very well, dish out punishment covered by brief

indicators.note: covered by means held inside another piece

parts.note: to brief someone is to inform them
to fine someone is to dish out a monetary punishment

explanation.surface: A judge, fine as ever, imposes a penalty a lawyer has set out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a noun, a lawyer's case, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In fine form is an idiom for performing very well.

clue.text: Savage flower

definitions.meaning: ... Savage was the drag persona of the British comedian Paul O'Grady

explanation.surface: A wild bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a flower, and Lily Savage was a famous British drag act, so the surname clues the first name.

clue.text: It hurts to wear jewellery in this game

indicators.note: to wear is to have on, so one piece is worn inside the other

parts.note: bling is flashy jewellery
ow is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A sport where wearing jewellery is painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling is a sport, a game of rolling balls at pins or bowling in cricket.

clue.text: Note about covering musicians

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added at the end
a layer is a covering

explanation.surface: A memo about cover versions for a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a musical note, but it is a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Players perform on instruments, so they are musicians.
